full_judgment: 11. Mr. Mahbub Ali, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the respondent submitted that that neither the Court of Settlement nor the High Court Division sitting in its writ jurisdiction can decide/ adjudicate the disputed question of facts as have been raised by the plaintiff therefore, the Civil Court is the only forum to redress grievances of the plaintiff as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He further submitted that since, the case before the Court of Settlement was not filed within the stipulated period of limitation nor the original judgment of the Court of Settlement was found in the record therefore, judicial record was tampered with and fraud was practiced upon the Court of Settlement in having the property excluded from 'Ka' list and as such, without holding inquiry and trial and without thrashing out the allegations in the plaint it cannot be rejected. He further submitted that neither the High Court Division nor the Appellate Division decided the issues raised in the plaint on merit and the jurisdiction of the Civil Court is still open to thrash out the allegations. He submitted that the principles of res-judicata in writ matters, where decisions are made in a summary proceedings mostly on affidavits, it should not be applied with the same strictness as in disputes in suits or proceedings determined in Civil Courts. He submitted that since, the defendant-appellant obtained the judgment from the Court of Settlement suppressing the fact of the title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit property and willfully and deliberately did not make the plaintiff a party in the proceedings nor the Government disclosed the fact of selling the property to the plaintiff by registered deed dated 08.11.1990 and delivered possession to him therefore, in any way the judgment of the Court of Settlement was not binding upon the respondents. He submitted that Government action in contesting the writ petition as well as filing of Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2186 of 2001 feeling aggrieved only to the extent of imposing penalty at the rate of 20% interest on the rent in no way can be said to have been decided the matter finally rather, the conduct of the Government as well as the appellant in contesting the proceedings is clearly collusive one which are liable to be adjudicated in the Civil Court.
